title: Smooth sliceness and four-ball genus obstructions

items.title: Integral intersection lattice of a simply connected four-manifold
items.statement: Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold. Its integral intersection lattice is the abelian group $L_X=H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$ with the integer-valued symmetric bilinear pairing $Q_X(\bar x,\bar y)=\langle \operatorname{PD}^{-1}(x)\smile\operatorname{PD}^{-1}(y),[X]\rangle$. Here $\operatorname{Tor}$ is the subgroup of elements of finite order, $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation class, and $\operatorname{PD}:H^2(X;\mathbb Z)\to H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the Poincaré duality isomorphism. The rank is $b_2(X)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(X;\mathbb Q)$. The lattice is positive definite when $Q_X(x,x)>0$ for every nonzero $x\in L_X$; it is unimodular when a Gram matrix in an integral basis has determinant $1$ or $-1$.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds

items.title: A full-rank unimodular sublattice has index one
items.statement: Let $n\ge1$, let $L$ be a free abelian group of rank $n$ with an integer-valued symmetric bilinear form whose Gram determinant is $1$ or $-1$, and let $f:L\to\mathbb Z^n$ be an isometric homomorphism, where $\mathbb Z^n$ has its standard dot product. Then $f(L)=\mathbb Z^n$.

references.title: Shalom Eliahou and Eitan Shalom, Number Theory course notes
references.locator: Appendix, Proposition 1.1, printed pp. 57–58; index of a full-rank integer sublattice equals absolute determinant

items.title: The integral intersection pairing is unimodular for a simply connected four-manifold
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold with $\pi_1(X)=0$. Its integral intersection lattice on $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$ is a finite-rank free abelian group and its intersection pairing is unimodular.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: Theorem 1 and §I.2, printed pp. 280–282; integral intersection form convention, with unimodularity proved locally from PD and UCT

items.title: Sign-fixed self-dual moduli and deformation setup
items.statement: Let $X$ be a closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold and let $P\to X$ be a smooth principal $SU(2)$-bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. The Hodge star on two-forms is $*$, and $F_A^-=(F_A-*F_A)/2$ denotes the anti-self-dual projection of the curvature of a connection $A$. The equation used in this item is $F_A^-=0$, so the curvature is self-dual; this convention and the negative second Chern number are fixed together for the positive-definite orientation. The self-dual moduli set is the set of smooth connections satisfying $F_A^-=0$, modulo the action of smooth gauge transformations of $P$. At a solution, the deformation complex is $0\to\Omega^0(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\xrightarrow{d_A}\Omega^1(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\xrightarrow{d_A^-}\Omega^-(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\to0$, and its gauge-fixed operator is $D_A=d_A^*\oplus d_A^-$. For index calculations, $D_A$ is completed from the first Sobolev space of one-forms to the direct sum of the zeroth Sobolev spaces of zero-forms and anti-self-dual two-forms.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §§I.2 and II.1, printed pp. 282–287; sign convention $F_A^-=0$ and $c_2(P)[X]=-1$

items.title: Intersection lattice of a four-manifold with rational-homology-sphere boundary
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold whose boundary $M$ is a rational homology three-sphere, meaning $H_*(M;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. The boundary intersection lattice has underlying group $L_W=H_2(W;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$. Poincaré–Lefschetz duality identifies each $x\in H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$ with a class $\alpha_x\in H^2(W,M;\mathbb Z)$. Define $Q_W(\bar x,\bar y)=\langle\alpha_x\smile\alpha_y,[W,M]\rangle$, where $\smile$ is the relative cup product and $[W,M]\in H_4(W,M;\mathbb Z)$ is the relative orientation class; equivalently, this is the signed intersection number of interior two-cycle representatives. Its rank is $b_2(W)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(W;\mathbb Q)$. A nondegenerate positive-definite $Q_W$ is called a positive-definite filling lattice. It is not required to be unimodular; the boundary linking form can make its determinant have absolute value greater than one.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §3.3, Poincaré–Lefschetz duality for manifolds with boundary and cup-product pairing, printed pp. 252–255

items.title: Index formula for the sign-fixed self-dual deformation operator
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold, let $b_1(X)=\dim H^1(X;\mathbb R)$, let $b_-(X)$ be the dimension of the negative subspace of its real intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be a smooth principal $SU(2)$-bundle. Put $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. For the real Fredholm operator $D_A=d_A^*\oplus d_A^-$ from first Sobolev one-forms with values in $\operatorname{ad}P$ to zeroth Sobolev zero-forms and anti-self-dual two-forms, its Fredholm index is $8k-3(1-b_1(X)+b_-(X))$. In particular, if $\pi_1(X)=0$, the intersection form is positive definite, and $c_2(P)[X]=-1$, then $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}(D_A)=5$.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §§I.2 and II.1, printed pp. 282–287; the index-five case for $c_2(P)[X]=-1$ and $b_1=b_-=0$

items.title: The boundary intersection pairing is well defined and rationally nondegenerate
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with rational-homology-sphere boundary $M$. The signed intersection pairing on interior two-cycles descends to a symmetric integer-valued bilinear form on $H_2(W;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$, this group is free of finite rank, and the form is nondegenerate after extending scalars to $\mathbb Q$. The form need not be unimodular.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §3.3, Poincaré–Lefschetz duality for manifolds with boundary and cup-product pairing, printed pp. 252–255

items.title: The E8 lattice is even unimodular and is not diagonal
items.statement: For the rank-eight lattice $L_{E_8}$ with Gram matrix $C$ specified in its definition, the form is positive definite, has determinant $1$, and takes even values on every vector. It has no vector of squared norm $1$, so it is not isometric to the standard diagonal lattice $\mathbb Z^8$ and admits no isometric full-rank embedding into that lattice.

references.title: Tim Perutz, Lectures on Gauge Theory and Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: §24, pp. 119–126; E8 lattice comparison, with the carrier supplying a direct matrix verification

items.title: Taubes existence of an irreducible self-dual instanton on a positive-definite four-manifold
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a compact simply connected oriented smooth four-manifold with a Riemannian metric whose intersection form is positive definite, and let $P\to X$ be a principal $SU(2)$-bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. For the equation $F_A^-=0$ in the stated orientation convention, the moduli space contains an irreducible smooth connection. The conclusion is existence for the given metric and bundle; it does not assert that every connection is irreducible or that the unperturbed moduli space is regular.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §I.5, printed285–286; exact existence conclusion and Proposition5 correction interface; the full construction is supplied locally

items.title: Topological realization of the E8 intersection form
items.statement: Assume full AC. There exists a closed connected simply connected oriented topological four-manifold $Y_{E_8}$ whose integral intersection form is isometric to the positive-definite even unimodular lattice $L_{E_8}$. This is a topological realization statement and does not assert a smooth structure on $Y_{E_8}$.

items.title: Generic regularity and orientability for the sign-fixed self-dual moduli problem
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented Riemannian four-manifold with positive-definite intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be an $SU(2)$-bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. Complete the connections in $H^3$ and the gauge transformations in $H^4$, and use the unbased irreducible configuration quotient. The curvature section $\Phi([A])=F_A^-$ takes values in its $H^2$ equation bundle. Choose an open subset $U$ covered by finitely many bounded Coulomb slice balls centered at smooth irreducible connections, and an open $V$ whose closure is contained in the union of strictly smaller closed balls in these charts, their images lying in $U$.

Allow smooth gauge-equivariant perturbation sections supported in $U$, whose slice representatives are smooth $H^3$-valued maps with finite uniform $H^3$ norm on the specified chart balls. Interpret them in the $H^2$ equation bundle by inclusion. Give this class the topology of the uniform $H^3$ section norm on those finitely many balls together with convergence of the section and its slice derivative $H^3\to H^2$ uniformly on compact subsets. The perturbations for which $\Phi+\sigma$ is transverse to zero at every zero in $\overline V$ form an open dense subset. Their zero sets in $V$ are smooth orientable five-manifolds, and the real determinant line of the gauge-fixed deformation family is orientable on the irreducible quotient. The based quotient may be used to pull back this orientation; it carries an additional $SO(3)$ framing fiber and is not the unbased five-dimensional moduli space.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §§II.1–II.4, printed pp.288–295; complete slice, bounded smoothing perturbation, and determinant orientation proofs

items.title: Uhlenbeck compactness and removable singularities for self-dual connections
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold, let $P$ be a fixed principal $SU(2)$-bundle with charge $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$, and let $(A_j)$ be smooth connections satisfying $F_{A_j}^-=0$ and $\sup_j\int_X|F_{A_j}|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}<\infty$. Then a subsequence, bundle isomorphisms, and a finite set $S\subset X$ exist such that the transported connections converge in local Sobolev gauge on compact subsets of $X\setminus S$ to a self-dual connection on a possibly lower-charge bundle of charge $k_\infty$. For each $p\in S$ there is a positive integer bubble charge $m_p$, and $k=k_\infty+\sum_{p\in S}m_p$. The limiting connection extends smoothly across every puncture after gauge transformation, and the compactified moduli space is obtained by adjoining the lower-charge limits together with the finite bubble points and their integer charge labels.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §§III.1–III.2, printed pp. 295–302; compactness, bubbling, and removable singularities

items.title: Reducible ends and compactification of the one-instanton moduli space
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold with positive-definite intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be an $SU(2)$ bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. Use the unbased $H^3/H^4$ quotient and the determinant-line orientation. There is a compatible perturbation procedure as follows: prepare the finitely many reducible circle-slice obstruction maps by arbitrarily small equivariant finite-rank smoothing perturbations, and make a further generic bounded smoothing perturbation on finitely many bounded irreducible slice collars in a middle region. The procedure is fixed near the prepared reducibles and vanishes on the entire small-instanton end. The further choices may be made arbitrarily small; they form a relatively open dense transverse class on the prescribed smaller middle collars.

The resulting regular irreducible zero set is an oriented five-manifold. Its ideal completion is compact, has one small-instanton boundary stratum identified with $X$, and has exactly the finitely many prepared reducible cone points, with no other strata. A neighborhood of each cone point is a cone on $\mathbb{CP}^2$. Delete smaller open cone neighborhoods and add the small-instanton boundary. The result is a smooth compact oriented five-manifold with boundary $X$ and one projective-plane link for each actual reducible orbit, with their induced orientations. Each projective link has one of the two complex-orientation signs; no common sign or numerical spectral-flow computation is asserted. The orientation on the component with the small-instanton end can be chosen so that this boundary is $X$ with its given orientation. The number of projective links is at most $b_2(X)$.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §§II.1–II.4 and III.3–III.4, printed pp. 287–294 and 302–315; reducible slices, spectral flow, and Taubes end

items.title: Donaldson diagonalization theorem for positive-definite four-manifolds
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a compact connected smooth simply connected oriented four-manifold. If its integral intersection form is positive definite, then there is an integral basis of $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$ in which the form is the identity matrix. Equivalently, the integral intersection lattice is isometric to the standard diagonal lattice $\mathbb Z^{b_2(X)}$ with dot product.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: Theorem 1, printed p. 280; complete argument §§I.2–I.5, II.1–II.4, III.1–III.4 and Appendix

references.title: Tim Perutz, Lectures on Gauge Theory and Symplectic Geometry
references.locator: §24, pp. 119–126; independent Seiberg–Witten/Elkies route, comparison only

items.title: A slice-branched-cover gluing produces a closed definite four-manifold
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot such that its double branched cover $M=\Sigma_2(K)$ is a rational homology sphere. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper embedded disk with boundary $K$, and let $B_D$ be the connected double cover of $B^4$ branched over $D$. Let $W$ be a compact connected smooth simply connected oriented four-manifold with boundary identified orientation-compatibly with $M$, and assume its boundary intersection form is positive definite. Assume also that the image of $\pi_1(M)\to\pi_1(B_D)$ normally generates $\pi_1(B_D)$, meaning its normal closure is the whole group. Then the oriented gluing $X=W\cup_M(-B_D)$ is a closed smooth simply connected positive-definite four-manifold, and inclusion induces an isometric full-rank embedding $Q_W\hookrightarrow Q_X$ of integral intersection lattices with $b_2(X)=b_2(W)$.

references.title: R. H. Fox and J. W. Milnor, Singularities of 2-spheres in 4-space and cobordism of knots
references.locator: Introduction, smooth slice-disk convention, pp. 258–259; the local gluing construction is proved from the repository rational-ball-cover lemma, van Kampen, and Mayer–Vietoris

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, An Application of Gauge Theory to the Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: Theorem 1 and §I.2, closed smooth simply connected positive-definite target and intersection-form convention

items.title: A non-diagonal filling lattice obstructs smooth sliceness under the gluing hypotheses
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot whose double branched cover $M=\Sigma_2(K)$ is a rational homology sphere. Suppose $M$ bounds a compact connected smooth simply connected positive-definite four-manifold $W$ with boundary intersection lattice $Q_W$ of rank $n$. Assume $Q_W$ has no isometric full-rank embedding into the standard dot-product lattice $\mathbb Z^n$. If every smooth proper slice disk $D$ for $K$ has a branched-cover boundary inclusion $\pi_1(M)\to\pi_1(B_D)$ whose image normally generates $\pi_1(B_D)$, then $K$ is not smoothly slice. This conditional obstruction gives no numerical lower bound on the smooth four-ball genus beyond excluding genus zero.

title: Smooth sliceness and four-ball genus obstructions — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: E8 as the lattice input to a conditional sliceness obstruction
items.statement: Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and suppose its double branched cover bounds a compact simply connected positive-definite smooth four-manifold $W$ whose boundary intersection lattice is isometric to $L_{E_8}$. Then this particular filling lattice has rank eight and has no isometric full-rank embedding into the standard lattice $\mathbb Z^8$. This verifies the algebraic nonembedding input for the conditional KT-26 sliceness obstruction. It does not assert that a specified knot has such a filling, that every slice-disk branched cover satisfies boundary normal generation, or that the conditional obstruction proves any further numerical four-ball-genus bound.

items.title: The topological E8 manifold does not satisfy the smooth diagonalization conclusion
items.statement: Under full AC, every closed connected simply connected oriented topological four-manifold with positive-definite integral intersection form has that form isometric over the integers to the standard diagonal lattice.
